posts.body:
Hello, RPG Makers!
I've been wanting to do a (kind of?) minigame that also works in battle.
I have an example from the final boss in "Kirby Star Allies",
the void termina fight.
specifically the end part of the boss.
[I placed the link at the part I mentioned.]
The basic mechanic is that to "win" the minigame, you spam a button repeatedly.
that's it. but in Kirby, there's animations that play in the background.
the video might explain more.
because I can't really describe it.
is there any plugins that could help?
can it be done using just regular events?
any help would be appreciated.

posts.author: buuward
posts.body:
If you want to make a visually appealing minigame, you'd need to get plugins no doubt. I'm sure there are many free minigame plugins you can find out there (QTE from joyful being an example) that are like this, but if you can't find one (I couldn't, either) you'll have to do commands.
If you want to achieve this with normal commands outside of battle, you can have an action button activated event that increases a variable by 1 until it hits a set amount like 10. You can have a passive event in the background slowly decreasing the variable by 1 if you want resistance. You can probably make it look as good as you want this way, as you have animations, events and the map to your disposal. You can have the sprites or the map change depending on what the variable is with conditional branches, so maybe you can make a beam similar to the kirby video.
If you want to do it mid battle, you can either abort it for the minigame, or do it with choices. Since there are no event placements, you'll have to go with choices if you don't want to find scripts.
What this does is display a choice over and over that increases a variable by 1 until you either reach 10 or reach -1 by a passive decrease. You can use this as a switch condition in troops. Of course, this would look ugly, but it will work as a spam one button minigame during battle with no scripts.
I'd recommend you do it outside of battle though. (You'll have to add a loop, and a break loop for when you win or lose. I forgot that because I'm used to it just automatically repeating if the switch is still on)
Plugins would probably do this minigame better, but this is a good backup if you can't find any. I wish you luck on your game!
EDIT:
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/inde...g-button-minigame-in-rpg-maker-vx-ace.153045/
the first reply in this thread explains a way you can do this without scripts. It will probably work better than mine, and it most likely will work in MV if you wish to use it.
